props.text: Meta Model API is an inference API for the latest models from Meta, including Muse Wonder and Muse Spark, and Muse Code is a coding agent built for Muse Spark. Call the API to build your own app or agent, or run Muse Code for a ready-made agent in your terminal — same models, same auth.

props.text: Muse Wonder takes text, image, video, audio, and PDF input, returns text, has a 1,048,576-token context window, and supports reasoning effort levels from "minimal" to "max". Muse Wonder comes in two variants. Muse Wonder is on Model API and in Muse Code. Muse Wonder Full, the higher-capability variant, is available only in Muse Code with a subscription, so setting reasoning effort to "max" on Muse Wonder doesn't select it.

nodes.label: Chunk
nodes.name: Muse Spark is Meta's model for agentic and coding work, such as multi-step ...

props.text: Muse Spark is Meta's model for agentic and coding work, such as multi-step tool loops, software engineering assistants, and long-context reasoning. All Muse Spark versions take text, image, video, audio, and PDF input, return text, and have a 1,048,576-token context window. Muse Spark 1.3 is the latest version, tuned for agentic workflows (multi-step tool, browser, and long-horizon tasks) with improved coding over 1.2. Muse Wonder and Muse Spark take the same requests on the same endpoints, so moving a workload between them is a model ID change.

props.text: Audio understanding in Muse Spark 1.3 is not fully supported, and response quality for requests that include audio may be degraded. For audio, use Muse Spark 1.2, or Muse Voice Transcribe for dedicated speech-to-text.

props.text: Muse Voice Transcribe is Meta's speech-to-text model on Meta Model API. Reach Muse Voice Transcribe two ways: the realtime WebSocket endpoint (wss://api.meta.ai/v1/asr/realtime) for live audio, or the file endpoint (POST /v1/asr/transcribe) for a recording you already have.

props.text: Muse Spark Open is the open-weight release of Muse Spark: an 816B-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 42B active parameters. Instead of calling it over Model API, you download the BF16 or NVFP4 checkpoint and serve it on your own GPUs with a runtime such as SGLang or vLLM, or call it through a hosted inference provider.
